Thank you for your hard work, and we sincerely hope you’ll consider this feedback.

Best regards,
A loyal FragPunk player

Fragpunk, my beloved. I have been on a kick lately of trying all the free-to-play tactical shooters out there, including Valorant. Fragpunk has been BY FAR the one that has held my attention the longest, with its stylish abilities, great TTK, and amazing gunplay. The heroes feel like they've been well-thought-out, and barriers to entry aren't too high, unlike other tactical shooters. 

Unfortunately I can't at this time recommend it, as the game went from over 100,000 players to now just around 1000, and the devs don't seem interested in reviving it. One thing they do is match you with entirely bot lobbies without telling you, instead of just giving you a slightly longer wait. 

It's a deeply unoptimized Unreal Engine game with persistent ping and lag issues (even for people using ethernet) -- the devs have "addressed" this by offering a token for 6 months of some "FPS-boosting" software with their referral code. 

It feels like this game is going to break my heart. I can't stop myself from logging in to play, because the stylishness and game design are top-notch. But I can see the writing on the wall.

But, I noticed in the story comics (for their individual backstories) included for the playable characters it includes genuine digital art. (They also put a lot of writing for event stories as well which I appreciate as well.) So, I think if they already have that implemented more it should be more showcased in the stickers & profile decorations as well. Basically, there's a mix of both genuine digital art & AI.

I took a break from the game for a while, and when I came back I barely recognized it. Despite the fact that many new servers were added, it honestly feels like they switched to cheaper hosting overall. Why do I say that? Because the character models in the game feel even faster than before, but if you analyze demo recordings and look closely at hit registration, you can clearly see opponent models lagging.

On top of that, the hit registration has become absolutely awful. This used to be one of the things that set the game apart from other shooters. In my personal ranking it used to be number one for hit registration, followed by Valorant and then CS2.

The player base also feels much smaller now, which is not surprising considering the issues I mentioned. Replacing players with bots in different modes is simply ridiculous. The bots are clearly unfinished — they can kill poor newcomers while being completely blinded, for example. From the outside they even look like blatant cheaters because their aim sticks to you when they shoot. Watching it in demos is honestly cringe.

What is even more noticeable is the quality of character skins and weapon skins. It feels like most of the game’s budget and development time is going into cosmetics. Yes, everything looks beautiful, but what’s the point when there’s nobody to play with (except bots), and when the game barely functions properly when you finally do get real opponents?

Then there’s crossplay with console players. In about 70–80% of my matches, those poor console players are just struggling to even aim at people in time, not to mention using abilities properly.

If you’re wondering about ranks — I’ve tried them all. I’ve been PunkMaster, Master, Diamond, and Platinum, and it’s the same everywhere. I even tested it on my second account, and it’s exactly the same story.

As for skins, I also tried the gacha system and got a good feel for its randomness and somewhat predatory design. I pulled the top skins for Pathogen and Crown, but in both cases I had to completely roll through the banner to get them. It honestly felt like a Genshin Impact simulator. Sure, they occasionally throw you some freebies and basic skins, but all the top-tier items are very expensive.

The only thing I can genuinely praise is the battle pass. If you buy it once and don’t spend the currency on anything else, you can keep renewing it indefinitely. Were you expecting something else? Of course not — the only real upside is tied to battle pass money. Everything else follows the same monetization philosophy.

Finally, the anti-cheat. It’s basically a scarecrow in a field — maybe it scares the crows a little, but they still eat the corn and crap all over your garden. In other words, it’s complete garbage, even though it runs at the kernel level.

I had huge hopes for this game. At the beginning it looked amazing. But now it just feels like another disappointment. Aside from the old, worn-out shooters, there’s honestly nothing new worth playing right now — because FragPunk has turned into a complete mess.

I should also mention that this game has a smoother and more polished gameplay experience than Valorant.

This may be a long review but its my genuine look on this game and I feel people should take it for consideration when playing.

Fragpunk deserves more credit than it is given. The gameplay is enjoyable with good gunplay and character mechanics that all feel well balanced. 

The main negative reviews ive seen are mainly about ai generated content, bots-cheaters, and micro transactions 

As for ai content. The only content I can tell would be the showcase picture of skins. for example the battle pass banner for 2 premium skins. other than that the art in the game is great and has a lot of character. Stickers for example would be the guess for ai use. but i cant tell and I enjoy a lot of them. I can care less if a game uses a little ai if its done right. They shouldnt get a negative review for that. 

Bots and Cheaters. Ive been going through ranked and have not experienced any bots or cheaters. now for casual and arcade idk, but so far its been fun. Play with friends to get the most out of the arcade game modes, there a great addition for casual play and are well made. They added a tower defense game mode with around 100 or more cards just for it and I was suprised how fun it was.

Now for Micro Transactions. By far the most important because people give the most negative reviews about it.
Upfront im going to say Fragpunk is by far one of the best games to do micro transactions right and Ill explain why. 

First lets address free content. ill use the current season events for example. You get 3 character skins and 4 weapon skins 25 ultra pop cans with stickers, charms, head and arm ornaments, and profile stuff for free. Now these skins have different variants and vfx, different sound effects, cross hairs, tracers, and animations. I like how even rare and epic skins look good and make me want to use them instead of letting them rot. Not to mention you can use stickers and charms to make your own skins. I added a animated flaming sticker to my knife, last game to come close to that was bo3 and i miss it, but fragpunk brought it back. Ive even gotten random free promos that gave me ultra pop cans and frag coins. the premium currency, a free character unlock and a battle pass voucher thats $10 free.

Which brings me to the currencies of the game.
 GOLD- used to unlock lancers, fuse stickers for higher rarity up to legendary animated ones. and some event spins
 GLUNITE- to unlock some skins and get normal pop cans but these cans have a chance to drop ultra pop cans
FRAGCOINS- You buy this currency. But promos and events can give some. This event gives you 600 for free. Mind you the battle pass is 900 and a legendary skin is 968.

The battle pass gives you 900 for the next one and its easy to climb. 5 weapon skins 2 lancer skins and 18 ultra pop cans. 
again variants with vfx and animations

Now Paid stuff. legendary skins are 986 lancers and melee are 1986. every legendary comes with sound vfx, bullet tracers, reload animations, kill and popup vfx, and inspect animations. There is a TL;DR at the end. I have spent more time than I would care to admit on this review, but I put in the effort because FragPunk is actually a good game that seems to be in the wrong hands. This review was originally roughly twice as long, but I had to cut a lot because of Steam’s character limit.

✅ SHARD CARDS ARE ABSOLUTELY THE HIGHLIGHT OF THE GAME

Shard Cards change how the rounds function and really set FragPunk apart from its competition. They can give you anything from small benefits in the background, such as damage and fire rate increases, to large changes that completely affect how you approach the round. For example, "Blade Master" is a card that gives you a sword that blocks bullets from the front, forcing enemies to shoot your feet or your back.

✅ GREAT CHARACTER DESIGNS, SKINS, AND COSMETICS

The character designs are genuinely good, and the higher-tier skins are very high quality. They are similar to the expensive, higher-tier skins in Valorant. They look good, have good animations, and the sticker system is nice as well. Unfortunately, you cannot view most skins in-game once they leave the store, so newer players may only discover them by seeing other players using them. Some skins eventually return, but there does not appear to be any guarantee about when or if a particular skin will come back.

✅ SOLID GUNPLAY

FragPunk is similar to Valorant and Counter-Strike in terms of its objective, map design, and general gameplay. However, it doesn't have a counter-strafe mechanic, and its guns have consistent recoil patterns. This means you can memorize and learn to control the recoil patterns.

✅ GOOD MAPS

Most of the maps are good and work well with the game’s Shard Card system. They have their own identities, and the gameplay is generally fun across most of them.

✅ SURPRISINGLY FUN SIDE CONTENT

FragPunk also has side modes such as Toy Front Line and its related modes. They combine tower-defense elements with a Call of Duty Zombies-style survival mode and mix in mechanics from the Shard Card system. You survive multiple rounds, place defenses, and earn some pretty decent cosmetic rewards. The mode is fun for a few hours, but it becomes repetitive. These modes can become truly great if developed a bit more. I'd also like to highlight that COD zombies started as side content as well.

✅ SOLID RANKED SYSTEM

The ranked system is generally fine. It may be a little too easy to rank up, but I have seen worse systems in other games. Reaching the highest rank is still satisfying, and the rewards are fine, even if they are nothing crazy. It is good enough and serves its purpose.

❌ ROUTE FLAPPING AND CONNECTION PROBLEMS

I am not sure whether this is a server or routing issue, but some players constantly experience something called route flapping. It causes severe lag and can make the game practically unplayable. I personally do not have this problem, but I have friends who experience it, and I have seen other players complain about it as well. Even after extensive troubleshooting, it sometimes refuses to go away and only seems to happen on FragPunk.

❌ THE CHEATING PROBLEM IS COMPLETELY OUT OF HAND

This is easily the biggest problem with the game and the main reason I will probably stop playing soon. It feels like everyone is cheating, especially once you reach Diamond and the higher ranks.

I am not only talking about players using aimbots or wall hacks. Cronus Zens, no-recoil macros, scripts, and similar forms of cheating appear to be everywhere. Almost nobody seems to have recoil. In Diamond, it is common to see what appears to be half the lobby cheating. In Ace and Punk Master, the two highest ranks, you would be lucky to find even one player outside of your party who appears to be playing legitimately. It is that common for nearly the entire lobby to be using scripts, no-recoil macros, or similar cheats.

The cheating is not subtle either. Players can openly admit that they are cheating and still not get banned. I have personally had several players argue with me that using no-recoil macros and scripts is completely fine because “everyone” uses them at the higher ranks. I reported those players and it always turns up nothing.

I want to emphasize that these are not just players with good recoil control. They can use the guns with the most recoil in the game, yet their reticles have absolutely no bounce or movement. There is not even the slightest amount of give, and they never seem to make a mistake while controlling the recoil. Their aim can be terrible in every other way, but the reticle still remains perfectly steady.

If you're like me and have played a lot of shooters, achieving the highest ranks in them, and learned how to control recoil, you can tell the difference. What these players are doing is not consistent with legitimate gameplay. Their recoil control looks like world-class talent while everything else about their gameplay suggests otherwise.

Some people try to call these “legit cheats” because you supposedly still need to be good at the game. To put it in plain English, using no-recoil macros or devices in a tactical shooter is cheating, and you are not good if you need them to perform well.

❌ REPORTS SEEM TO ACCOMPLISH NOTHING

When you report someone, you receive a message saying that an investigation will begin shortly, but nothing ever seems to happen. I have reported close to 30 blatant players over the past two or three weeks without receiving a single notification that action was taken.

❌ THE ACTIVE PLAYER POOL IS EXTREMELY SMALL

At the time of writing, FragPunk has 344 Steam players online, a 24-hour peak of 897, and a 30-day average of around 600, compared to its all-time Steam peak of 113,243. The game is also bleeding roughly 100 to 300 average players each month.

The console population does not appear much larger, since the in-game scoreboard regularly shows balanced or mostly PC lobbies. This small player pool means repeatedly encountering the same people and cheaters at higher ranks.

❌ THE MENUS ARE A NIGHTMARE

The main menu is an absolute nightmare to navigate. There are a million different menus, pop-ups, events, currencies, and icons constantly being thrown in your face. It is not intuitive at all, and you may need to play for actual weeks before you can quickly find everything.

❌ THE MEMBERSHIP SYSTEM

Characters cost 18,888 Gold each and take a long time to unlock through normal gameplay. This grind clearly exists to push players toward the membership system.

The monthly membership costs $9.90 and includes the Premium Battle Pass and access to every character, but only while the membership remains active. The annual membership costs the equivalent of $8.33 per month, paid upfront, and includes the Battle Pass. Its main benefit is permanently unlocking every current and future character, even if you never renew the membership.

❌ THE MONETIZATION IS RIDICULOUS

FragPunk has loot boxes called Curiosity Pop Cans that can contain featured knife skins. The skin has a 0.01% overall drop rate, while the 100-material reward has a 0.99% drop rate. A skin costs 1,000 materials, and an Ultimate drop is guaranteed every 50 cans, meaning you could potentially need 500 cans to earn one. Buying that many would cost around $706 before tax, even after including the one-time discounted seasonal bundles. No cosmetic should cost anywhere near that much.

⭐ FINAL RATING: 6.5/10

Even with all of its issues, the most important part of any game is whether it's fun and has good gameplay. FragPunk is very fun. It is genuinely a great game, but it has a lot of significant problems that ruin the actual gameplay experience and drag it down. This game easily has the potential to be a 9/10 and could possibly even be a 10/10 in the right hands.

TL;DR: A great game inspired by CS and Valorant, ruined by cheaters and bad Eastern monetization.

Let's start off by saying that I absolutely recommend FragPunk.

Even though FragPunk is not as popular as other games in the genre, it is the most fast-paced and fun one in my opinion. For one, the "shard card" system allows creative gameplay - every round can be played different based on the shard cards chosen by the team.

However, like any other game FragPunk does have problems - mostly the overwhelming amount of gamemodes. Apart from the regular gamemode (called Shard Clash), there are several TDM modes, the Outbreak mode (a zombie vs. survivors kind of gamemode), duels, solo death matches etc.
While a big amount of gamemodes isn't necessarily a problem, it is to be acknowledged that most of these modes are rarely played. 

Considering that the amount of gamemodes is the only major negative point I can think of, while being able to mention several positive points (e.g. fun gameplay, short rounds, nice graphics, a mostly nice community) I fully recommend playing FragPunk, especially with friends!

Genuinely one of the best competitive shooters I have ever played

Generally reaching the top rank in a game is an absolute slog and painful. Hitting champ on R6 years ago took a mental toll, hitting Pred on Apex broke me and made me uninstall after getting it, etc. Reaching Punkmaster on Fragpunk was genuinely fun the ENTIRE way through. Every game feels different with the card system, and it's the only shooter where you continually see players doing things and causing interactions with abilities and cards that make you stop and think "why didn't I think of that?" or "wow, that's cool".

I'm really not sure where the review bombers come from that call it a cash grab or Valorant clone, when in reality the only thing it shares in common with Valorant is that it is a 5v5 bomb mode. There are a TON of games like that, and this game does a good job carving a unique identity in that genre. You'll also notice EVERYONE who says those things have under 20 hours, and this game takes 50+ to really start to grasp and get used to. The cash grab accusations are braindead, considering the only paid things are cosmetics, and everything can be earned for free with enough playtime. If you don't have the self control to not spend money on every pretty skin you see, maybe stick to single player games, as Fragpunk's microtransactions are objectively less predatory than games like Apex, Overwatch, CS2, Valorant, etc.

The real shortcoming of this game is the marketing team. Please for the love of god advertise this game, do a collab, SOMETHING. This game has SO much potential behind it, and it is being wasted by a marketing team who clearly has no idea what they are doing. Also, who decided this game needed a "Hentai" tag??? There is ZERO nudity or sexually suggestive material, the most you'll see is a character's midriff or thigh. Is this middle school? If you are like me and have the "Hentai" tag blocked from showing up on steam recommendations, this game would never appear for you unless searched for directly.

tldr; Great game, awful marketing team, review bombed by low play time Valorant dudes who are mad they cant find any 15 year olds to groom
Quality gameplay, actual fun, relatively clean lobbies and decent balancing a lot of the time.

FragPunk brings a fresh twist to the hero shooter genre with its fast-paced gameplay, vibrant visual style, and unique Shard Card system that changes the rules of every match. The gunplay feels responsive, matches move at a thrilling pace, and the card mechanics create unpredictable moments that keep rounds exciting.

At its core, FragPunk has all the ingredients of a standout competitive shooter. The weapons feel satisfying, the characters are distinctive, and the constant gameplay variety helps it avoid feeling repetitive.

Unfortunately, the game's biggest weakness is its apparent reliance on bots. Many players have reported matches that feel filled with AI-controlled opponents rather than real competitors. Whether these bots appear in beginner lobbies, casual matchmaking, or other situations, their presence can make victories feel hollow and raise questions about the competitive integrity of the experience.

When you're matched against real players, FragPunk shines. The strategic use of Shard Cards combined with quick gunfights creates some genuinely memorable moments. However, it's difficult to fully invest in the competition when you're unsure if the enemy team is made up of actual players or scripted bots.

Despite this issue, the game remains fun for those seeking a casual shooter with a unique identity. The foundation is solid, and if the developers continue improving matchmaking transparency, FragPunk could become a much stronger competitor within the hero shooter market.

Pros
- Fast and engaging gunplay
- Creative Shard Card system
- Stylish visuals and presentation
- Matches rarely feel repetitive

Cons
- Bots can make matches feel artificial
- Competitive experience lacks trust and consistency
- Victories sometimes feel less rewarding

Final Score: 7/10
FragPunk is a creative and entertaining shooter with excellent gameplay foundations, but the perception of bot-filled matches prevents it from reaching its full potential. Great ideas and plenty of fun are here, but the multiplayer experience needs more authenticity to ensure long-term success.
